title: Customer orders
what: The customer clicks BUY NOW for a pair of sneakers. Payment and an order record begin the workflow.
payer: The customer pays the retailer; the retailer pays its service providers.
revenue: Product sale; providers may earn processing or software fees.
entry: Learn order workflows or serve retailers with useful software.

title: Order management
what: The order is validated and sent to the operation responsible for shipping.
payer: Retailer pays internal labor or contracted software/service fees.
revenue: Software subscriptions or contracted service fees.
cost: Integrations, support, exceptions and data security.
entry: Study the difference between an order record and a shipment.

title: Inventory located
what: The requested sneaker size is matched to available inventory at an appropriate location.
payer: Retailer or brand pays inventory/warehouse service providers.
revenue: Storage and inventory-service fees or internal operations.
cost: Stock control, space, counts and software.
entry: Learn inventory accuracy before offering custody services.

title: Fulfillment
what: The facility releases the order for physical preparation.
who: Retailer fulfillment team or contracted fulfillment business
payer: Brand pays the fulfillment provider when outsourced.
cost: Space, labor, software and service management.
entry: Pilot a narrow order profile with clear service terms.

title: Pick
what: A worker or automation retrieves the correct sneaker SKU and quantity.
payer: Brand pays through fulfillment fees or internal payroll.
entry: Learn SKU verification and safe material handling.

title: Pack
what: The sneakers are protected in packaging suitable for transport.
payer: Brand pays packaging and handling costs under its agreement.
revenue: Packing services and agreed packaging charges.
cost: Materials, labor, benches and damage prevention.
entry: Practice packaging and define quality checks.

title: Label
what: A shipping label connects the box to a carrier service and destination.
payer: Shipper pays carrier postage/service and any software fees.
revenue: Shipping software fees; transport fees are a separate obligation.
entry: Learn address, service and tracking reconciliation.

title: Warehouse / fulfillment facility
what: The prepared box waits in outbound staging within the facility. These steps often occur in one building.
payer: Brand pays contracted services or operates the facility itself.
cost: Lease, labor, utilities, safety and security.

title: Sortation
what: The box is grouped with other parcels headed toward the same outbound lane.
payer: Shipper/carrier pays the operator according to its network agreement.
cost: Sort systems, space, staff and incorrect-sort rework.
entry: Learn scan and custody controls at handoffs.

title: Distribution
what: The network stages and directs shipments toward destination regions.
payer: Retailer, network or contracted customer pays the service provider.
cost: Regional facilities, staff, systems and transfers.
entry: Map one regional network and its customers.

title: Middle-mile transportation
what: A vehicle moves grouped shipments between facilities.
payer: Shipper, network or intermediary pays the transport provider.
revenue: Lane, trip, mile or dedicated-capacity fees.
cost: Vehicle, fuel, driver time, tolls and empty miles.
entry: Verify transport requirements and round-trip lane economics.

title: Local delivery facility
what: The box reaches the destination-area operation and is assigned to delivery work.
payer: Network or shipper funds the operation.
revenue: Facility/handling contract or internal network activity.
cost: Space, staff, scans and dispatch systems.
entry: Understand check-in, allocation and custody transfer.

title: Last-mile carrier
what: The contracting delivery business accepts responsibility for the assigned service.
payer: Prime carrier, shipper or retailer pays under its agreement.
revenue: Route, stop, package or negotiated service fees.
cost: Drivers, vehicles, insurance, dispatch and working capital.
entry: Request verified onboarding requirements and model a route.

title: Route
what: Parcels are organized into a planned sequence of stops. Packages and stops are different counts.
payer: Carrier pays staff or software providers.
revenue: Dispatch services, software or included carrier operations.
cost: Software, coordination, waiting and exception handling.
entry: Practice route planning without assuming every package is a stop.

title: Driver
what: The driver completes the safe physical delivery and required proof of delivery.
who: Employee driver or appropriately classified operator
payer: Employer pays wages, or contracting party pays agreed services.
revenue: Labor compensation or owner-operated service fees.
cost: Time, vehicle costs where applicable, phone and safety.
entry: Verify pay, expense responsibilities and delivery procedures.

title: Customer
what: The customer receives the sneakers; delivery records close the outbound handoff.
payer: Delivery payment normally follows the business contract, not a payment at the door.
revenue: Completed service is reconciled for invoicing.
entry: Learn what counts as accepted delivery in the agreement.

title: Returns / reverse logistics
what: If the sneakers are returned, transport and inspection lead to a restock or other authorized disposition.
payer: Retailer/brand pays agreed return services; customer policies vary.
revenue: Return transport, inspection, handling or recovery fees.
cost: Pickup, inspection, storage, rework and disposition.
entry: Define custody, condition grading and permitted handling.
